sources.entry: HyperSwitch ⚠ - Payment switch to make payments fast, reliable and affordable. Connect with multiple payment processors and route traffic effortlessly, all with a single API integration. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: Hyperswitch is an Apache-2.0 licensed, Rust-based open-source payments switch that routes transactions across many payment processors through a single API integration, with optional modules for vaulting, retries, routing, and reconciliation.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a modular payments infrastructure: an app server (Rust) that connects to 100+ payment processors such as Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Worldpay, and Checkout.com, with smart routing and retry logic. Optional modules named in the README cover cost observability, revenue recovery (intelligent retries), a PCI-compliant vault (including bring-your-own-vault for VGS and TokenEx), intelligent routing, automated 2-way and 3-way reconciliation, and drop-in alternative payment method widgets such as PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna. A Control Center dashboard is provided for configuring connectors, routing rules, and viewing logs. The ecosystem also includes separate repos for web, Android, iOS, React Native, and Flutter checkout SDKs, plus Terraform and Helm deployment tooling. A local Docker setup script and a hosted sandbox are mentioned.
use_cases: replace a single-PSP payment gateway integration
recover failed recurring payments with smart retries
store customer cards in a PCI-compliant vault
embed checkout in web or mobile apps
how_to_run: Choose a deployment profile: Standard, Full, or Minimal (script detects Docker/Podman)
Open the access links printed at the end of setup
Configure a connector and test a payment
notable: Single API integration fronting 100+ payment processors
Modular: pick only vault, routing, retries, reconciliation, or observability modules
Bring-your-own-vault support for existing VGS or TokenEx stores
One-click local Docker setup script with Standard, Full, and Minimal profiles
Official client SDKs for web, Android, iOS, React Native, and Flutter
caveats: The README describes it as a commercial open-source stack, and some modules appear to be part of a paid Payment Suite offering; pricing and tier details are not given in the README
Cloud deployment is via Helm charts for AWS, GCP, or Azure, with the instructions linked externally rather than included
Connector coverage is described as 100+, but the README only lists five connectors in its table
